t: This is the monument to Thomas Bayes and his family, in Islington. It marks a vault holding members of the Bayes and Cotton families. The most famous of them is Thomas Bayes, who lived from 1702 to 1761. He was a Presbyterian minister and a mathematician, and is remembered as a statistician and philosopher for formulating a particular case of the theorem that now carries his name, Bayes' theorem. So the stone in front of you commemorates a quiet clergyman whose idea is still used today.
